findings.title: `AssignmentSource.queued` is evaluated once at import time
findings.description: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, so it runs when the class body executes (module import), not when an instance is created. Every `AssignmentSource` built in a process carries that process's startup time, including the ones from `from_integration` (assignment_source.py:21-25). Nothing reads `queued` today: a repo-wide search for `AssignmentSource` and `assignment_source` finds no reader. The impact is latent, but the field is serialized into every task payload through `to_dict()`, and the name suggests it should record when the assignment was queued. `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so the bug is not caught. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` or set the value explicitly in `from_integration`.

findings.title: Status-sync contract gained an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller supplies
findings.description: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares `assignment_source`, but its only caller, src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43-46, never passes it. That caller also invokes `should_sync("outbound_status")` without a source, so the loop guard does not apply to status sync. `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py:161) no longer matches the abstract signature because it has no `**kwargs` and no `assignment_source`. On the assignee side, `assignment_source` is forwarded to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:59-61), but the Jira, Jira Server, and VSTS implementations absorb it through `**kwargs` and never read it. Either remove the unused status parameter or wire it up, and state in the PR whether status loops are a follow-up.

findings.title: No test covers the "other integration still propagates" path or the task's source parsing
findings.description: The new test covers only the same-integration case and asserts `assert_not_called`. That assertion is meaningful because the sibling `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign` uses the same setup and does enqueue a sync. However, the comment at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:387-389 says other integrations should still propagate, and no test checks that. There is no case where `sync_source.integration_id` differs from this installation's id and the sync runs. `should_sync(attr, sync_source)` and the `assignment_source_dict` parsing at src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-61 have no direct tests. Add a positive case with a second integration as the source.

findings.title: The wire format changes for every outbound assignee sync, not only inbound-originated ones
findings.description: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` always includes `assignment_source_dict` in the task kwargs, set to `None` when there is no source. A worker still running the old three-argument task signature would raise `TypeError` on each such message during a rolling deploy. The `retry` wrapper (src/sentry/tasks/base.py:163-172) re-queues on `Exception`, so the effect is delayed syncs. Work is lost only if old workers outlive the retry budget. Omitting the key when it is `None` avoids the mismatch for the common case.

findings.title: `from_dict` silently returns `None` on bad input
findings.description: When the payload does not match, `from_dict` returns `None`, and the caller at src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56 treats that the same as "no source". The loop guard then turns off with no log. Only schema drift should trigger this, so the risk is low, but a log line in that branch would make the failure visible. Also, `from_dict` does no type checking (`integration_id="abc"` is accepted), and the `ValueError` in the except clause cannot come from a dataclass constructor, which raises only `TypeError`.

findings.title: Naming and small consistency drift
findings.description: The parameter is `sync_source` in `should_sync` but `assignment_source` everywhere else. `from_integration` calls `AssignmentSource(...)` directly (assignment_source.py:22) while `from_dict` uses `cls(...)`. The test name `test_from_dict_inalid_data` (tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:13) has a typo.

findings.title: The loop guard compares the correct identifiers
findings.description: The check `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` uses fields that exist. `RpcIntegration` has `id` and `name` (src/sentry/integrations/services/integration/model.py:20-24), and `RpcOrganizationIntegration` has `integration_id` (model.py:57). The check runs after the `key is None` and `org_integration is None` guards, so it cannot dereference `None`. Both the inbound assign and deassign paths pass a source (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:94-116).

findings.title: Task kwargs and imports are compatible with existing code
findings.description: Example (example/integration.py:152), Jira (jira/integration.py:936), Jira Server (jira_server/integration.py:1038), and VSTS (vsts/issues.py:217) all accept `**kwargs`, so the new keyword is accepted. The Celery serializer is pickle (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741), so the `datetime` inside `to_dict()` serializes without error. Every `should_sync` call outside the new code passes a single argument. The module-level import in src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:15 does not create a cycle, because `src/sentry/integrations/services/__init__.py` is empty.
